clue.text: Prompt cat bites tail of mouse and departs

indicators.note: a cat that bites something holds it between its jaws, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: feline is a word for a cat

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs, as on a timetable

explanation.surface: A cat catches a mouse by the tail and then leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning quick; it is a noun, the cue an actor is fed.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre, a cue fed to a comic by a straight man is a prompt for the punchline.

clue.text: Whip caught on short thick cord

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a rope is a thick cord

explanation.surface: A whip has been snagged on a stubby length of heavy cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding whip with a short stock and a loop is the jockey's or rider's whip.

clue.text: Track over in wood

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A trail that runs across through the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A track on a record is a spiral channel cut in the vinyl, a cut line or rut.

clue.text: Studio flat one's mates discovered first

indicators.note: first puts the uncovered letters at the front of the charade
dis-covered: with its cover, the outer letters, stripped off

parts.note: a lier is one who lies flat

explanation.surface: A studio apartment whose sharers were found first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studio flat' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Studio' alone; 'one's' is 'one has', joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or designer's workshop is a French loan word for a studio.

clue.text: Fully engages mariners with balls

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, sailors
orbs are spheres, balls

explanation.surface: Sailors playing with balls are completely occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wholly takes up your attention grips you completely.

clue.text: Need American backing to cut waste left by European

indicators.note: to cut into means one piece breaks into the other
left by means the European letter departs from the waste word

parts.note: inefficiency is wastefulness

indicators.note: backing turns the American abbreviation round

explanation.surface: A demand for US money to reduce European extravagance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by European' means the letter E departs from the waste word before the reversed American letters cut in.
explanation.definitionFit: Need in the sense of lack or shortage: not having enough of something.

clue.text: Biting and corrosive about Republican

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: an acid is corrosive

explanation.surface: A description of a sharp-tongued, scathing Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something sharp and pungent, or a cutting, bitter remark.

clue.text: Certified that English education should miss nothing when reviewed

indicators.note: re-viewed: looked at again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
should miss means the letter for nothing is dropped from education

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: An official confirms that schooling in England will skip nothing at inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop O from EDUCATION, then shuffle THAT + E + EDUCATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A document confirmed as genuine has been verified and officially vouched for.

clue.text: Source of disco beat remained

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: to welt is to beat, leaving weals

explanation.surface: The thump from the disco hung on in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived or stayed somewhere is past tense of a verb meaning to reside or linger.

clue.text: Waits to enter society where singles may get less attention?

definitions.text: where singles may get less attention?

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bides means waits, as in biding one's time

explanation.surface: Wallflowers join a club where single people get overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests unattached people at a dance; the singles are records.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vinyl single the flip side carries the lesser track, which gets far less airplay.

clue.text: Get to press naked cherub's bottom

parts.note: a putto is a naked cherub in Renaissance art
a bed is the bottom of a river or sea

explanation.surface: A tabloid instruction to print a picture of a nude cherub's behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper jargon: an edition is finished and sent off for printing when it is ready to go.

clue.text: Strengthening bond, following lead given by fine men

indicators.note: following means the bond word comes after the rest

parts.note: a rein is a lead for a horse
F is short for fine, as on pencils
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men
cement is something that bonds

explanation.surface: Strong ties form after an example set by good men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' joins the lead to the fine men.
explanation.definitionFit: Strengthening a structure or force means adding support or extra troops to it.

clue.text: Strict foreign soldier in purge

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to rid is to purge
a GI is an American soldier, foreign to a British setter

explanation.surface: A harsh overseas soldier carrying out a purge.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbending or inflexible, as with strict rules that allow no exceptions.

clue.text: Slave personnel regularly picked out

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals picks every second letter of the word

explanation.surface: A slave whose staff were routinely singled out.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Saxon labourer or serf, a crossword stalwart for a slave.

clue.text: Half of awning closed round bar

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is three letters, here the back three
round means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a door pulled to is closed

explanation.surface: Half the awning was shut around the pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast block of gold or silver is a bar of metal.

clue.text: Pro-Americans starting meetings

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Supporters of the USA are starting gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of forum: public places or gatherings where matters are discussed.

clue.text: Front and back blown off prison wing, perhaps

parts.note: fore means front

indicators.note: the back, or last letter, is blown away

parts.note: limbo is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A prison wing whose front and rear walls were destroyed by explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wing' looks like part of the prison; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's wing is an example of an arm or leg at the front of the body.

clue.text: National American vessel, one that's managed to go about

indicators.note: to go about means to surround, so one piece wraps the others

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
USS is the prefix for a United States Ship
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A US ship with someone who managed to turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country; this is one of Russia.

clue.text: Team spirit beat dire prospects

indicators.note: beat means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Morale in the squad overcame a bleak outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for the shared pride and loyalty of a group's members.

clue.text: Declined to live over a postgraduate?

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: be means to exist, to live
a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, so its holder is one who is past graduation

explanation.surface: Someone refused to share a home with a graduate student.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'postgraduate' as a holder of a degree, a BEd, rather than a further-degree student.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide going out has fallen away, so it has receded or decreased.

clue.text: Avoiding the dirt cheap evil Frenchman

indicators.note: evil means bad, corrupted, so the letters are rearranged
avoiding means the letters of the second word are left out of the shuffle

explanation.surface: A wicked, miserly Frenchman who keeps out of the muck.
explanation.walkthrough: DIRT CHEAP minus T, H, E leaves DIRCAP to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Picardy, the northern French region, is a Frenchman.

clue.text: Does one sailor start to spot fish around north and south?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
around means the fish wraps the compass letter

parts.note: cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a sailor begins seeking fish across the hemispheres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does one' is British slang for clears off, does a runner; it looks like the start of a question.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang 'do one' means leave quickly, as a runaway flees in secret.

clue.text: Spoils Posh Spice, perhaps following opening of show

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Victoria Beckham (Posh Spice) is a WAG, a footballer's wife or girlfriend

explanation.surface: Posh Spice spoils a show by arriving after it starts.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG is British tabloid slang for the wives and girlfriends of footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot or plunder, the goods a thief carries off, are the spoils.

clue.text: Boozer on time for picture

indicators.note: on means the boozer comes after, set on the time letter

parts.note: an alkie is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk takes the time to pose for a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British for a pub, but here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: An early sound film was a picture, as in going to the pictures.

clue.text: Trot round during race

indicators.note: round means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a Trot, a Trotskyist, is a red
by means during, as in by night

explanation.surface: A horse trots around during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, run at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous horse race at Epsom, or any big sporting contest between rivals.

clue.text: Bemoan somehow about onset of Delhi belly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters wrap the other
somehow means in some other way, so the letters are rearranged
onset is the start, the first letter

explanation.surface: Complaining in some fashion about the first signs of a traveller's stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delhi belly' is slang for traveller's diarrhoea; 'belly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Belly and tummy are everyday words for the stomach region of the body.
